_comment: ShellTerra OldTownLandmarks seed data — timemark format. `date` is each landmark's founding year (YYYY-01-01). One landmark per line.
_source: Public sources (Wikipedia, SOHO, CA State Parks). Coordinates verified 2026-09-07; SHP-building coords reused from the OldTownActivities feed.
_verify_before_running: HELD — do not seed yet. Pending: (1) app pulled, (2) discriminator field name confirmed, (3) `entry_type` attribute added to the timemarks collection, (4) one line added to buildTimemarkDoc to write it. `entry_type:"landmark"` below is provisional.
kind:"timemark" routes these to the timemarks collection. Set SHELL_ID=6a9f709e2f5727bfb643 before seeding.
After seeding, flip the shell public + is_seeded (is_private:false, public_override:true, is_seeded:true) like OldtownActivities.
date = founding year. Old Town SHP uses 1769 (settlement founding, its historical significance) rather than 1968 (park established) — flip if you'd rather anchor on the park date.
Serra Museum (7) and Heritage County Park (11) coords are slightly rounded; the 4 SHP buildings (1,8,9,10) are exact from the activities feed.

items.title: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park
items.description: Preserves the site of California's first European settlement, recreating San Diego's Mexican and early-American era (1820s-1870s) with original and reconstructed buildings.

items.title: Whaley House Museum
items.description: Greek Revival brick home built by Thomas Whaley in 1857; once a courthouse, theater, and store, and long reputed one of America's most haunted houses.

items.title: El Campo Santo Cemetery
items.description: One of San Diego's oldest cemeteries, a Roman Catholic burial ground from 1849 holding pioneers, Californios, and the outlaw Yankee Jim Robinson.

items.title: Cosmopolitan Hotel (Casa de Bandini)
items.description: Built in 1829 as Juan Bandini's adobe home and expanded by Albert Seeley in 1869 into a stagecoach hotel; today a restored hotel and restaurant.

items.title: Casa de Estudillo
items.description: Built in 1827, one of California's oldest surviving adobes and a National Historic Landmark, later famous as "Ramona's Marriage Place."

items.title: Mormon Battalion Historic Site
items.description: Interactive museum commemorating the Mormon Battalion's 2,000-mile march to San Diego during the Mexican-American War, 1846-47.

items.title: Junipero Serra Museum
items.description: Spanish Revival museum opened in 1929 on Presidio Hill, overlooking the site of California's first mission and presidio, founded in 1769.

items.title: Mason Street School
items.description: San Diego's first public schoolhouse, a one-room wood-frame building from 1865 restored on its original site.

items.title: Robinson-Rose House
items.description: An 1853 commercial and residential building that once held county offices and a newspaper; now the park's visitor center.

items.title: Seeley Stable
items.description: A reconstruction of Albert Seeley's 1869 stagecoach stable, housing a collection of wagons, carriages, and Western artifacts.

items.title: Heritage County Park
items.description: A county park preserving relocated Victorian-era buildings from the 1880s, including San Diego's first synagogue.
